A. K. M. Shafiqur Rahman -For the Petitioner. 
Mozammel Hoque Buhiyan-For the Respondent.
parties:
M/s. Hotel Safina Ltd ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Commissioner of Taxes, (formerly) the Commissioner of Income tax) 
Chittagong Zone, Chittagong ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Ruhul Islam, J.-This is a reference under section 66(2) of the Income-Tax Act, 1922. The assessee preferred an appeal on 10th May, 1969 before the Appellate Assistant Commissioner, A- Range, Chittagong, against the order of assessment made on 1st April, 1969 for the assessment year 1968-1969. The Appeal was rejected in limine on 13th November 1969, on the ground that the appellant did not pay one-half of the sum demanded under section 29 of the Income-Tax Act. The demand was made of assessment amount of Rs. 44,528/- which consists of income tax demand of 38,128 and penal interest of Rs. 6,400/-. The appellant paid Rs. 19,129/- only two arch the demand. The assessee preferred Second Appeal before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal on the ground that the Appellate Assistant Commissioner was not justified in rejecting the appeal in limine merely on technical ground without going into the merits of the appeal, although the assessee complied with the requirement of section 30 by paying Rs. 19,129/-. The Appellate Tribunal also dis missed the appeal by the order dated 10th September, 1970 on the finding that the assessor's case clearly fell within the mischief of the first proviso to section 30 of the Income-Tax Act, and, as such, in the facts and circumstances of the case the Appellate Assistant Commissioner was justified in not entertaining the appeal. Thereafter, the asses-see filed" an application before this. Court under section 66(2) of the Income Tax Ace for a direction upon the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal to state the case for answering the questions as framed therein. On this application a Division Bench of this Court by an order dated 29th May 1975 directed the Income Tax Tribunal to state the case for answering the question as framed in the order. The question as framed is as follows: 

 "Whether on the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the Income-tax Amendment Ordinance XVI of 1959, the Appellate Tribunal was right to hold that the Assistant Commissioner was justified in not entertaining the appeal." 

 "No appeal under this sub-section shall be against any order unless (i) one half of the cum demanded under section 29 on an assessment in respect of which the assessee intends to prefer an appeal under this section or the tax payable on the basis of the latest previous year in respect of which he has been assessed under section 23 and in respect of which no appeal under this section or section 23 is pending, whichever is the less or (ii) the tax payable by him under section 22A, whichever is the greater, has been paid provided further that the Central Board of Revenue may, upon an application made in this behalf, in any case, modify or waive the requirement of the first proviso. 

 4. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that appeal was preferred on 10th May, 1969 but the same was taken up for hearing by the Appellate Assistant Commissioner after the Ordinance XVI of 1969 came into force, that is on 1st July, 1969. Since the provision of law requiring deposit of 50% of the sum demanded was no longer in existence at the time of hearing of the appeal, the Appellate Assistant Commissioner instead of rejecting the appeal in lit nine should have entertained the appeal as an appeal properly filed. In support of his sub-mission the learned Advocate referred to a decision of the Supreme Court of India in the case of Commissioner of Income-Tax Bombay City I Vs. Filmiest an Ltd. I.T.R. 42 (SC) 163. This decision, how-ever, does not support the argument advance by the learned Advocate, in as much as, the question for consideration in the reported decision was as to whether an appeal filed within time but with insufficient deposit should have been treated as properly filed one if the deposit was made after the period of limitation. In our opinion the decision instead of supporting the contention of the assessee rather supports the stand taken by the Department. We find it difficult to accept the submissions made by the learned Advocate that the question as to whether he appeal was properly filed or not should have been considered with reference to the law in existence at the time when the appeal was taken up for hearing, because the appeal being in order according to the law as existing on the date when the appeal was taken up for bearing, the Appellate Assistant Commissioner was not justified in rejecting the appeal in Jiminy on the ground that it was not filed properly. Since the Ordinance was not made retrospective, there is hardly any scope for advancing this argument. It has been rightly pointed out that the assessee could have applied to the Central Board of Revenue for modification or waiver of the requirement of the first proviso to section 30, but no such step was taken by the assessee. There is no doubt that in view of the expression "the sum demanded" occurring in the first proviso to section 30 as it stood when appeal was preferred on 10th May, 1969, the deposit of a sum of Taka 19,129/- was not sufficient to meet the requirement of law. In the facts and circumstances of the case we feel that the question as framed requires some modification. Accordingly the question is framed in the following manner: 

 Whether in the facts and circumstances of the case the appeal filed without complying with the requirement of the first proviso to section 30 of the Income-Tax Act could be entertained in view of amendment of section 30 by the Ordinance XVI of 1969? 

 5. For the purpose of determining whether the appeal complied with the requirement of the law, the Appellate Assistant Commissioner was to be guided by the law which was in existence when the appeal was filed and not the law in existence when the appeal was taken up for consideration, unless the law was made retrospective. However, the appeal could be saved if the amendment was made within the period of limitation for filing appeal. But this is not the case of the assessee. 

 6. In view of what has been stated above the question are answered in the negative. We make no order as to cost. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner prays for a certificate under section 66A sub-section (2) of the Income Tax Act. We do not consider it a fit case for appeal to the Supreme Court. Therefore, certificate as prayed for is refused.
